curriculum: The 2026–27 Dutch-medium degree permits up to one-third of teaching in English. Annex 4 and the student major show eight compulsory first-year courses (60 EC), 30 EC across the four courses in one chosen track, 15 EC of major electives, three 5 EC final-year courses and a 15 EC thesis. The major totals 135 EC and profiling is 45 EC. The example takes Migration and Global Development, first in both the student major page and formal track list. The 2026–27 calendar rules out Storytelling for Open Cities (formerly Planning for Open Cities) in period 1 slot B and Transport Geography in period 2 slot A, because they share slots with the required theory and themes courses respectively. Planning Theory (period 1 C, GEO2-7011) and Geography, Representation and Media (period 2 C, GEO3-3405) are major electives in Annex 5 with distinct slots and no stated additional entry requirement in the corresponding minor lists. The year-two track and major electives account for 45 EC. Two remaining year-two slots and a first semester in year three can be filled with 15 and 30 EC of profiling respectively. At least 15 profiling EC must be at level 2 or above. The selected major has 45 EC at level 2 and 52.5 EC at level 3. The non-credit tutorial and study-career activities are listed separately by the calendar.
progression: Article 4.2 requires participation in both first-block courses and passing one before Borders in Perspective. Track entry requires 45 earned EC, passing Globalization and Development, and participating in Spatial Data and Geographic Information and Socio-Spatial Research. Themes follows participation in Theory. The mixed-methods project follows participation in Themes and requires a pass in Spatial Data and Geographic Information. The practice atelier requires participation in Theory and Themes and a pass in one. All four track courses are taken in one academic year, with period and slot sequence 1B, 2A, 3D and 4D. Before Analysis, students pass the mixed-methods project. Before Research Design, they pass the first-year courses and complete the track. Before the thesis, they also pass Research Design and participate in Science and Society and Analysis. The final-year calendar puts the three 5 EC components in period 3 and the thesis in period 4. The student calendar is an illustration of current ordering and slots; it does not guarantee future offerings.

Participate in Cities in Transition and Competing Claims on Space, and pass at least one of them before taking this course.
Theories and Approaches to Migration and Global Development

Start the track after earning at least 45 EC, passing Globalization and Development and participating in Spatial Data and Geographic Information and Socio-Spatial Research. Take the four track courses in one academic year.
Global Migration and Development: Key Themes
Participate in the track theory course before taking this course.
Participate in the track themes course and pass Spatial Data and Geographic Information before starting the project.
Participate in both the theory and themes courses and pass at least one of them before starting the lab.
Choose 45 EC of electives, with at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above. Options include an eligible minor, study abroad or a placement.
Pass the Mixed Methods Research Project before taking Analysis.
Pass the eight first-year courses and complete the track before taking Research Design.
Pass the eight first-year courses, all four track courses and Research Design, and participate in Science and Society and Analysis before starting the thesis.
